questions.stem: Why does React require a stable `key` on list items?
choices: To match elements across renders so component state and DOM nodes are reused correctly
questions.explanation: Keys are React's identity hint. With stable keys, reorders preserve component state and minimise DOM churn.

questions.stem: Which is correct?
choices: setCount(c => c + 1) avoids stale state when multiple updates batch in one event
useState batches synchronously across event loops
questions.explanation: Functional updaters receive the latest queued state, so two setCount calls in one handler increment by two.

questions.stem: An effect with deps [] runs:
choices: Once after first commit, cleanup on unmount
questions.explanation: Empty deps means React thinks nothing the effect uses changes, so it runs once and cleans up on unmount.

questions.stem: When does `React.memo` help?
choices: When a child is re-rendered by a parent but its props are unchanged by reference
Only when there are no hooks
questions.explanation: memo skips re-render if shallow-equal props match. It does nothing if props are new objects each render.

questions.stem: How does the reconciler treat a position where the component type changed (e.g. <Header/> became <Banner/>)?
choices: Unmounts the old subtree and mounts a fresh one (state is lost)
questions.explanation: Different types are not compatible. React tears down and re-creates; that's why preserving identity matters.

questions.stem: Which violates the rules of hooks?
choices: Calling useEffect at the top of a function component
Returning early after all hooks have been called
questions.explanation: Hooks must be called unconditionally in the same order each render so React can match them by index.

questions.stem: An effect fetches data and updates state. The user navigates between ids quickly. Without protection, what bug appears?
choices: Stale fetch resolves last and overwrites newer data
questions.explanation: Without a cancel flag or AbortController, the slow earlier response wins the race.

questions.stem:
Predict renders. Clicking only the input twice triggers how many App renders?

function App() { const [s, setS] = useState(''); return <input value={s} onChange={e => setS(e.target.value)} />; }
questions.explanation: Each onChange calls setS with a new string, scheduling a re-render. Two keystrokes → two re-renders.

questions.stem: useMemo is best used to:
choices: Cache an expensive computation across renders or stabilise a referential prop
questions.explanation: useMemo recomputes only when dependencies change. Don't reach for it for cheap computations — overhead outweighs benefit.

questions.stem:
What does this effect do?

useEffect(() => { document.title = name; });
choices: Runs after every render (no deps array)
questions.explanation: Omitting the deps array means React runs the effect after every render. Usually a bug; specify a deps array.

questions.stem: Why is `key={index}` problematic when items can be reordered?
choices: On reorder, items at the same index swap identities and React mismatches state / DOM
questions.explanation: If you insert at position 0, every old item's index shifts. React treats them as 'same key', applying wrong state to wrong row.

questions.stem: Which is true about JSX?
choices: It is syntactic sugar over React.createElement calls
It must be in a separate file
questions.explanation: JSX compiles to function calls. Browsers don't understand it directly — a build step (Babel/swc) is required.

questions.stem: How do you read the latest state inside an event handler scheduled by useEffect?
choices: Use a ref (useRef) or functional updater
questions.explanation: Closures capture the state at the time the effect ran. useRef gives a live mutable cell; functional setters receive latest.

questions.stem: What happens if useEffect's cleanup is omitted on a subscription?
choices: Subscriptions leak across re-renders and unmounts, eventually leading to duplicate handlers and updates on unmounted components
questions.explanation: React re-runs effects on dep changes and never auto-unsubscribes. You must clean up explicitly.

questions.stem: Which prop pattern correctly forwards an event handler down?
questions.explanation: Pass the function reference. Adding parens calls it immediately and passes the return value (often undefined).

questions.stem: What does useCallback do?
choices: Memoises a function reference so it stays stable between renders when deps don't change
Schedules a callback for next render
questions.explanation: useCallback(fn, deps) is equivalent to useMemo(() => fn, deps). Useful when fn is a dep of an effect or memoised child.

questions.stem: Which is true about lifting state up?
choices: When two siblings share data, move the state to their nearest common ancestor and pass props down
questions.explanation: Lifting puts the source of truth above both consumers, who become controlled via props.

questions.stem: Why does React 18 use 'concurrent rendering'?
choices: To allow rendering work to be interrupted/prioritised so urgent updates (input) don't wait for slow ones
questions.explanation: Concurrent mode lets React split work into chunks and yield to the browser for high-priority updates like user input.

questions.stem: Inside a controlled input, the source of truth for the value is:
choices: React state (props.value drives the input; onChange updates state)
questions.explanation: Controlled = React owns the value via state. Uncontrolled = the DOM owns it and you read via refs.

questions.stem: What is the virtual DOM?
choices: An in-memory tree of element descriptions that React diffs against the previous tree before touching the DOM
questions.explanation: vDOM is a lightweight representation. Diffing it is cheap; only the resulting minimal DOM mutations are applied.

questions.stem: Which scenario is a strong fit for useReducer over useState?
choices: Complex state with multiple sub-values that update together via discrete actions
questions.explanation: useReducer centralises transitions in a pure reducer — easier to test and reason about than scattering setX calls.

questions.stem: Why must hooks be called in the same order on every render?
choices: React identifies each hook by its call index; reordering would mix up the state slots
questions.explanation: Hook order is the implicit identity. Conditional hooks would scramble which state belongs to which call.
Both setN calls capture the old n=0 and pass 1. Batched together, the final value is 1. Use setN(c => c+1) twice for 2.

questions.stem: What does the cleanup function inside useEffect run between?
choices: Before the next effect runs (or on unmount), giving you a chance to undo the previous effect
questions.explanation: When deps change, React first runs cleanup for the previous effect, then the new effect. On unmount, only cleanup runs.

questions.stem: Which is the right way to send data to a parent from a child?
choices: Call a callback prop passed down from the parent
Throw an event from the child
questions.explanation: Data flows down via props; events bubble up by invoking callback props the parent supplied. This keeps the unidirectional model.
